title: Obama’s forgotten late-term moves
gist: A Slow Boring mailbag teaser: Yglesias argues Romney, not Trump, broke with the Bush-McCain immigration approach, so Trump's success illustrates the value of moderation; he also criticizes late-Obama policy on three fronts (cut off by paywall).

insights.claim: It was Mitt Romney, not Donald Trump, who made the hard break with the Bush-McCain interest in comprehensive immigration reform with a path to citizenship; the Trump-Romney immigration policy gap was modest.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Reframes the GOP immigration shift as predating Trump; relevant to forecasting Republican policy direction.
insights.locator: It was Mitt Romney, not Donald Trump

insights.claim: Trump's success illustrates rather than refutes the benefits of political moderation: he moved to the center on Social Security, Medicare and marriage equality to neutralize Obama's best attacks on Romney, while being dragged down by personal misconduct.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: If centrist positioning wins, Democratic moderates may have an edge in 2026-28 elections.
insights.locator: core difference between the Slow Boring worldview

insights.claim: Romney or another decent person could easily have won with Trump's views on Social Security and Medicare, so Republicans wrongly rationalize scumbag behavior as the source of Trump's win.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Policy positioning, not character, is argued to drive electoral outcomes.

insights.claim: Yglesias criticizes late-Obamaism on three fronts, all of which made it harder for Hillary Clinton to win in 2016, though he considers the administration's handling of Black Lives Matter basically fine.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Historical lens on how a departing administration's positioning affects successor's electoral prospects.

insights.claim: Obsession with colonizing the moon or other planets is likely idiosyncratic to Elon Musk rather than widespread, though Yglesias admits he lacks a clear index of conventional wisdom.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Musk-specific space ambitions should not be read as mainstream demand.
